questions.question: What is the intermediate level in the Panchayati Raj Institutions called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Panchayat Samiti.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Panchayat Samiti **is the** intermediate level in the Panchayati Raj Institutions.**
 
• It is the** tehsil or taluka or block level of the rural local-self government system** in India.
 
• Panchayat Samiti at the block level is an Administrative Authority that is responsible for enforcing the law and carrying it into effect.
 
• They form the middle level of the Panchayati Raj Institutions in India.
 
• It acts as a link between Village Panchayats (Gram Panchayats) and Zila Parishad (District council).
 
• It was formalized in 1992 by the 73rd amendment to the Indian Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Panchayati Raj

 
 
• Panchayati Raj is the system of local self-government of villages in rural India as opposed to urban and suburban municipalities.
 
• It consists of the Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) through which the self-government of villages is realized.
 
• They are tasked with "economic development, strengthening social justice and implementation of Central and State Government Schemes including those 29 subjects listed in the Eleventh Schedule."
 
• ​Part IX of the Indian Constitution is the section of the Constitution relating to the Panchayats.
 
• It stipulates that in states or Union Territories with more than two million inhabitants there are three levels of PRIs:
 
 
• Zilla Parishad at the District Level
 
• Panchayat Samiti at the Block Level
 
• Gram/Village Panchayat at the Village Level

questions.question: Who founded the International Olympic Committee (IOC) in 1894?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Baron Pierre de Coubertin**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Baron Pierre de Coubertin** founded the International Olympic Committee (IOC) in 1894.
 
• The IOC is the supreme authority of the worldwide Olympic movement.
 
• It was created to revive the ancient Olympic Games and to promote friendship and cooperation among nations through sports.
 
• Baron Pierre de Coubertin is often referred to as the father of the modern Olympic Games.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens, Greece, in 1896.
 
• The Olympic Games are held every four years, with the Summer and Winter Games alternating every two years.
 
• The IOC is headquartered in Lausanne, Switzerland.
 
• The Olympic motto is "Citius, Altius, Fortius," which means "Faster, Higher, Stronger."
 
• The Olympic symbol consists of five interlocking rings, representing the five continents of the world united by Olympism.
 
• The Olympic Charter is the codification of the fundamental principles of Olympism, rules, and bylaws adopted by the IOC.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the Indian political party system?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Single party system**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India has a **multi-party system**, which means that multiple political parties can and do contest elections across the country.
 
• A **single party system** is a system in which only one political party is legally allowed to hold power, which is not the case in India.
 
• The presence of numerous political parties in India leads to the formation of coalition governments, especially at the central level.
 
• The **lack of effective opposition** and **factions and defections** are also features seen within the Indian political party system due to the diverse and fragmented nature of the electorate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Indian political party system is characterized by a high level of **political pluralism**.
 
• There are several national and regional parties that play significant roles in the political landscape of the country.
 
• The Election Commission of India oversees the electoral process to ensure free and fair elections across the country.
 
• The Indian Constitution provides for a democratic system of governance, ensuring the representation of diverse groups and interests.
 
• Coalition politics is a common phenomenon in India due to the multi-party system, especially in forming governments at both the central and state levels.

questions.question: In which of the following years did the first elected Parliament come into existence?

__
 
• In the year 1952, the first Elected Parliament with two houses came into being in India.

 
 
• The first general elections under the new Constitution were held during the year 1951-52.
 
• The first elected Parliament came into existence in April 1952.
 
• The Seventeenth Lok Sabha was held in May 2019.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__

 
• Indian Parliament is the supreme legislative body of India.
 
• The Indian Parliament comprises of the President and the two Houses -
 
 
• Rajya Sabha 
 
• Lok Sabha 
 
 
 
• Lok Sabha:
 
 
• 543 members are directly elected by citizens of India on the basis of a universal adult franchise representing Parliamentary constituencies across the country.
 
• It has a term of five years.
 
 
 
• Rajya Sabha:
 
 
• Rajya Sabha or the upper house is a permanent body not subject to dissolution.
 
• One-third of the members retire every second year and are replaced by newly elected members.
 
• Each member is elected for a term of six years.
 
 
 
• Session of Parliament :
 
 
• The period during which the House meets to conduct its business is called a session.
 
• The Constitution empowers the President to summon each House at such intervals that there should not be more than a six-month gap between the two sessions. 
 
 
 
• The President has the power to summon and prorogue either House of Parliament or to dissolve Lok Sabha.
 
• The Constitution of India came into force on January 26, 1950.

questions.question: When was the National Interim Government of India formed, under Jawaharlal Nehru?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2 September 1946**__.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__ **

__
 
• **The Interim Government, **established on **September 2, 1946**, marked the** final phase of British colonial rule **in India.
 
• Its principal objective was to function as a transitional administration until India achieved complete independence.
 
• Jawaharlal Nehru, a prominent freedom fighter and close associate of** Mahatma Gandhi,** spearheaded the Interim Government, holding the position of Vice President of the Executive Council.
 
• Key figures such as **Sardar Patel, Rajendra Prasad, and C. Rajagopalachari** were integral members of this administration.
 
• Despite its significance, the Interim Government encountered substantial challenges, including communal tensions, economic instability, and the imminent partition of India.
 
• Nevertheless, the Interim Government played a pivotal role in facilitating the transfer of power from British to Indian hands, laying the groundwork for the subsequent establishment of independent India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru** was a multifaceted Indian leader, known for his roles as an anti-colonial nationalist, statesman, secular humanist, social democrat, and author.
 
• Nehru emerged as a key leader of the Indian nationalist movement in the 1930s and 1940s, advocating for India's independence from British colonial rule.
 
• Upon India's independence in 1947, Nehru assumed the position of the country's first Prime Minister, serving for an impressive 16 years.
 
• During his tenure, he championed parliamentary democracy, secularism, and advancements in science and technology, significantly influencing India's evolution as a modern nation.
 
• In the realm of international affairs, Nehru pursued a policy of non-alignment, steering India clear of alignment with the two blocs of the Cold War. Beyond his political leadership, Nehru was also a respected author.

• They are advisory bodies aimed at promoting cooperation and coordination between states and the center.
 
 
 
• **Quasi-Judicial Bodies**
 
 
• Quasi-Judicial Bodies are institutions that have powers akin to those of the law courts but are not courts in a strict sense.
 
• They are established to adjudicate disputes, enforce regulations, and ensure compliance with laws within their specific domain.
 
• Examples include consumer forums, income tax appellate tribunals, and the Central Information Commission.

• Albert Venn Dicey, a British jurist, is renowned for his work on the concept of the 'Rule of Law' in his book "Introduction to the Study of the Law of the Constitution" published in 1885.
 
• Dicey outlined three main principles of the 'Rule of Law': the supremacy of law, equality before the law, and the predominance of legal spirit.
 
• The 'Rule of Law' doctrine emphasizes that no one is above the law, and all individuals and institutions are subject to and accountable to the law.
 
• Dicey's concept significantly influenced the legal systems of many democratic countries, including India, where the 'Rule of Law' is a fundamental principle enshrined in the Constitution.
 
• His work laid the foundation for the modern understanding of constitutional law and the protection of individual rights against arbitrary governance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Supremacy of Law:** According to Dicey, the law is supreme and no one is above it, including the government itself. This principle is crucial in preventing the abuse of power.
 
• **Equality Before Law:** Dicey emphasized that every person, regardless of status or position, is subject to the same laws and is entitled to the same legal protections.
 
• **Predominance of Legal Spirit:** Dicey argued that the constitution is not the source but the consequence of the rights of individuals as defined and enforced by the courts.
 
• **Indian Constitution and Rule of Law:** The Indian Constitution incorporates the principle of the 'Rule of Law' in its Preamble and the Fundamental Rights, ensuring justice, liberty, and equality to all citizens.
 
• **Judicial Review:** The concept of judicial review in India, which allows the judiciary to review and invalidate laws and actions of the government that violate the Constitution, is derived from Dicey's principles of the 'Rule of Law'.

questions.question: In which year did the Indian Constitution declare Hindi in Devanagari script to be the official language of the Union?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1949**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hindi in Devanagari script** was declared the official language of the Union of India in **1949**.
 
• This declaration is enshrined in **Article 343** of the Constitution of India.
 
• According to this article, Hindi in Devanagari script would be used for official purposes of the Union, while the international form of Indian numerals would be used for official purposes.
 
• The Constituent Assembly adopted this provision on **14th September 1949**, which is now celebrated as **Hindi Diwas** every year.
 
• The Constitution also allowed for the continued use of English for official purposes for a period of 15 years from the commencement of the Constitution, which could be extended by legislation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Constitution of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949** and came into effect on **26th January 1950**.
 
• It establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the longest written constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.
 
• The Seventh Schedule of the Constitution contains three lists which delineate the subjects under the Union, State, and Concurrent lists.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in Article 368.
